correctness.rationale: A transfer matrix with eigenvalues q-1 and -1 gives all two-point moments. Exact multiplication establishes the cyclic Green inverse; a rank-one update yields precision. Fourier positivity and \(b^n\ge n(b+1)-1\) with equality only at \((n,b)=(3,2)\) determine all singular cases. A strict elementary bound settles adjacent signs; c=(b-1)(-1/b)^n settles every nonadjacent sign. The derivation covers all integers n,q in the claim. Independent finite enumeration and exact-rational matrix multiplication passed 6605 assertions using the embedded verify.py; this is corroboration, not an infinite certificate.

originality.rationale: The asserted result is not the classical proper-coloring count or two-point function, but the all-size complete inverse-covariance identity, unique singular case and parity-controlled full-order linear partial-correlation signs for one marked color. Relevant primary full text and public mathematical result summaries were compared by statement and implication. Spatial-mixing and influence inequalities do not determine the exact inverse, multi-site Potts correlation results concern a different interaction, and chromatic transfer matrices treat partition functions. Existing precision results on other models do not entail cycle-coloring precision. Earlier implicit derivations are a genuine residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Classical Potts, graphical-model, or inverse-susceptibility texts might implicitly derive the precise projected finite-cycle rank-one correction without using the searched terms.
A search of available literature and mathematical records cannot establish first-ever priority or independence.
The inferred precision is a linear projection quantity and is not a characterization of conditional independence for binary observations.

value.rationale: A single observed color of a proper categorical coloring is a natural hidden-state coarsening. Despite local graph constraints, its full-order linear precision generically contains nonzero interactions between every nonneighbor, with a nontrivial exact parity reversal between odd and even cycles, a unique singular triangle and an exponential fill-in coefficient. The result supplies the entire signed matrix across a natural infinite two-parameter family, not a special numerical instance, and clarifies the difference between marginal and adjusted dependence.
